data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Present perfect, past simple, and tense contrast
data.learningTitle: Why this quiz matters for exams
learningPoints: Strengthens control of present perfect vs past simple distinctions.
Builds accuracy with since, for, already, and yet.
Improves narrative clarity in formal and semi-formal contexts.
Targets common mistakes tested in IELTS and citizenship exams.
Develops confidence when discussing experience and achievements.
ESOL B2 and aligns with IELTS 6.0–6.5 and TOEFL iBT 72–94 score ranges.

sections.summary: Use present perfect for life experience without specific time.
sections.explain: Present perfect is used for experiences when no specific past time is mentioned.

words.word: She has visited London several times.
She visited London several times last year.
She has visited London last year.

sections.summary: Past perfect for an action completed before another past action.
sections.explain: Use past perfect ('had' + participle) for the earlier past action: 'had finished'. 'has finished' is present perfect, and 'had finish' lacks the participle.

words.word: By the time I arrived, he had already finished the project.
By the time I arrived, he had already finish the project.
By the time I arrived, he has already finished the project.

sections.explain: 'Since' is used with present perfect to show starting point in the past.

words.word: She has worked here since 2020.
She works here since 2020.
She worked here since 2020.

sections.summary: Use present perfect with 'for' to show duration.
sections.explain: 'For' expresses duration and requires present perfect for ongoing situations.

words.word: They have lived here for five years.
They lived here for five years and still live here.
They are living here for five years.

sections.explain: 'Already' commonly appears in present perfect sentences.

words.word: I have already sent the email.
I already sent the email.
I have send already the email.

sections.summary: Use 'yet' in present perfect negative or questions.
sections.explain: 'Yet' is used in present perfect questions and negatives.

words.word: She hasn't finished her homework yet.
She didn't finish her homework yet.
She hasn't finished yet her homework.

sections.summary: Past perfect for the earlier of two past events.
sections.explain: The earlier past action takes past perfect: 'had left'. 'had leave' lacks the participle, and 'has left' is present perfect.

words.word: The train had already leave when we got to the station.
The train had already left when we got to the station.
The train has already left when we got to the station.

sections.summary: Use present perfect for recent actions with 'just'.
sections.explain: 'Just' is commonly used with present perfect for recent actions.

words.word: He has just arrived at the airport.
He just arrived at the airport.
He has arrive just at the airport.

sections.summary: Use present perfect for actions with present relevance.
sections.explain: Present perfect connects past actions to the present.

words.word: She has lost her passport, so she cannot travel.
She lost her passport, so she cannot travel.
She has lose her passport, so she cannot travel.

sections.summary: Contrast past simple with completed past time and present perfect with ongoing impact.
sections.explain: Past simple is used with finished time; present perfect connects to now.

words.word: I finished university in 2022, and I have worked in this company since then.
I have finished university in 2022, and I work here since then.
I finished university in 2022, and I worked here since then.
